pr_title: feat(medusa): Allow regexp in CORS configuration

comments.body: `str.split(",")` runs before the regex check, so a regex that contains a comma is cut in two and never becomes a RegExp. Example: store_cors = `/^https:\/\/shop{1,3}\.example\.com$/`. The split gives `/^https:\/\/shop{1` and `3}\.example\.com$/`. `buildRegexpIfValid` needs a closing delimiter followed only by flags, so neither piece matches and both fall back to plain strings (`packages/medusa-core-utils/src/build-regexp-if-valid.ts:3`). The origin then never matches, and nothing reports the failure. Every consumer of this function is affected: `packages/medusa/src/api/routes/store/index.js:30`, `packages/medusa/src/api/routes/admin/index.js:49`, and the plugin route files that call `parseCorsOrigins`. Splitting on commas that sit outside the regex, or documenting that regexes cannot contain commas, would avoid the silent failure.
